title: Josephus Deep Bloodlines (Esau → Agag → Haman, Herod → Armenia/Cilicia/Rome, Sparta–Abraham Charter & Cleodemus–Heracles) + Intercultural Alias Atlas

nodes.name: King Agag of Amalek (1 Sam 15; Josephus Ant. VI.7 pp.339–342)
nodes.role: Amalekite Monarch Descended from Esau → Eliphaz → Amalek
nodes.notes: Captured by King Saul and executed by Samuel; Pseudo-Philo Ch. 58 & Rabbinic Targum record Agag siring an heir before death whose line produced Haman the Agagite.

nodes.name: Hammedatha the Agagite (Father of Haman, Esth 3:1)
nodes.role: Amalekite Noble & Father of Grand Vizier Haman
nodes.notes: Amalekite-Agagite noble of the house of King Agag; father of Haman.

nodes.name: Haman ben Hammedatha the Agagite (Josephus Ant. XI.6.5)
nodes.era: 5th c. BCE (Susa / Persia — Josephus Ant. XI.6.5 p.618)
nodes.role: Grand Vizier of Xerxes I / Agagite-Amalekite Descendant of Esau
nodes.notes: Josephus explicitly calls Haman 'by birth an Amalekite' (Ant. XI.6.5) — connecting Esau's grandson Amalek and King Agag straight into the Achaemenid Persian court opposite Benjaminite Mordecai & Queen Esther!

nodes.name: Zeresh (Wife of Haman & Daughter of Tatnai, Esth 5:10; Targum)
nodes.role: Wife of Haman & Mother of His Ten Sons
nodes.notes: Advised Haman to erect the gallows for Mordecai; mother of Haman's ten named sons.

nodes.name: Phasael II (Son of Herod the Great & Pallas, Josephus Ant. XVII.1.3)
nodes.era: c. 15 BCE – 1st c. CE (Josephus Ant. XVII.1.3 p.1197)
nodes.role: Son of Herod I the Great by His 6th Wife Pallas
nodes.notes: Son of Herod the Great by Pallas, named after Herod's slain elder brother Phasael.

nodes.name: King Tigranes V of Armenia (Herodian Grandson, Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4)
nodes.era: c. 10 BCE – 36 CE (Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4 p.1196)
nodes.role: Esau/Idumean & Hasmonean King of Armenia Installed by Rome
nodes.notes: Son of Herodian Prince Alexander and Cappadocian princess Glaphyra; ruled Armenia as Rome's client king Tigranes V.

nodes.name: Prince Alexander II (Son of Alexander & Glaphyra, Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4)
nodes.era: c. 12 BCE – 1st c. CE (Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4)
nodes.role: Herodian-Cappadocian Prince & Father of Tigranes VI
nodes.notes: Younger son of Prince Alexander and Glaphyra of Cappadocia; father of King Tigranes VI of Armenia.

nodes.name: King Tigranes VI of Armenia (Son of Alexander II, d. after 68 CE)
nodes.era: c. 20–70 CE (Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4; Tacitus Annals XIV.26)
nodes.role: Second Herodian-Cappadocian King of Armenia
nodes.notes: Appointed King of Armenia by Emperor Nero; father of King Gaius Julius Alexander of Cetis/Cilicia.

nodes.name: Princess Iotape of Commagene (Daughter of Antiochus IV; Wife of C. Julius Alexander)
nodes.era: 1st c. CE (Commagene / Cilicia — Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4)
nodes.role: Commagene Royal Princess Married Into the Herodian House
nodes.notes: Daughter of King Antiochus IV of Commagene; married King Gaius Julius Alexander of Cilicia, joining Commagene and Herodian/Hasmonean lines.

nodes.name: King Gaius Julius Alexander of Cetis / Cilicia (Josephus Ant. XVIII.5.4)
nodes.role: Herodian King of Cetis in Cilicia & Roman Senatorial Progenitor
nodes.notes: Son of King Tigranes VI of Armenia; married Princess Iotape of Commagene and fathered Roman suffect consuls Gaius Julius Agrippa and Gaius Julius Alexander Berenicianus.

nodes.name: Consul Gaius Julius Agrippa (Quaestor of Asia, fl. 109 CE)
nodes.role: Roman Senatorial Descendant of Herod the Great & Mariamne I
nodes.notes: Elder son of King Gaius Julius Alexander of Cilicia and Iotape of Commagene; entered the Roman Senate.

nodes.name: Consul Gaius Julius Alexander Berenicianus (Suffect Consul 116 CE, Proconsul of Asia)
nodes.role: Herodian-Hasmonean Roman Consul & Proconsul of Asia
nodes.notes: Younger son of Gaius Julius Alexander & Iotape of Commagene; became Roman suffect consul (116 CE) and Proconsul of Asia (132/3 CE), fathering Julia Cassia Alexandra.

nodes.name: King Azizus of Emesa (1st Husband of Princess Drusilla, Josephus Ant. XX.7.1)
nodes.era: c. 20–54 CE (Emesa / Homs, Syria — Josephus Ant. XX.7)
nodes.role: Priest-King of Emesa Allied With the Herodians
nodes.notes: Accepted circumcision in order to wed Herod Agrippa I's daughter Drusilla, linking Emesa's royal priesthood with the Herodian house.

nodes.name: Tobias of Judea (+ Sister of High Priest Onias II, Josephus Ant. XII.4.2)
nodes.role: Patriarch of the Tobiad House & Brother-in-Law of Onias II
nodes.notes: Married the sister of High Priest Onias II; father of powerful Judean statesman Joseph ben Tobias.

nodes.name: Joseph ben Tobias (Chief Tax-Farmer of Coele-Syria, Josephus Ant. XII.4)
nodes.role: Nephew of High Priest Onias II & Tobiad Leader
nodes.notes: Won Ptolemy III/IV's royal tax-farming contract for Coele-Syria, Phoenicia & Judea; fathered 7 elder sons plus Hyrcanus by his niece (daughter of brother Solymius).

nodes.name: Hyrcanus ben Joseph the Tobiad (Builder of Qasr al-Abd, Iraq al-Amir)
nodes.role: Youngest Son of Joseph ben Tobias & Transjordanian Magnate
nodes.notes: Son of Joseph ben Tobias; built the monumental Hellenistic fortress-palace of Tyre/Qasr al-Abd east of the Jordan before Antioch IV's accession.

nodes.name: King Nabopolassar of Babylon (626–605 BCE, Josephus Against Apion I.19–20)
nodes.role: Founder of the Neo-Babylonian Empire
nodes.notes: Chaldean founder of the Neo-Babylonian Dynasty cited verbatim by Josephus from Berossus; father of Nebuchadnezzar II.

nodes.name: King Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon (605–562 BCE, Against Apion I.19)
nodes.era: 605–562 BCE (2 Kgs 24–25; Josephus Against Apion I.19–20)
nodes.role: Conqueror of Jerusalem & Builder of Babylon
nodes.notes: Son of Nabopolassar; captured Jerusalem (597 & 586 BCE), exiled King Jehoiachin, and married Median princess Amytis.

nodes.name: King Evil-Merodach / Amel-Marduk (562–560 BCE, 2 Kgs 25:27; Josephus Ag. Ap. I.20)
nodes.role: Son of Nebuchadnezzar II Who Released King Jehoiachin
nodes.notes: Son and successor of Nebuchadnezzar II; elevated exiled Judahite King Jehoiachin out of prison before being assassinated by brother-in-law Neriglissar.

nodes.name: King Neriglissar (Nergal-sharezer, 560–556 BCE, Jer 39:3; Josephus Ag. Ap. I.20)
nodes.role: Son-in-Law of Nebuchadnezzar II & Neo-Babylonian King
nodes.notes: Married a daughter of Nebuchadnezzar II and reigned 4 years after Amel-Marduk.

nodes.name: King Labashi-Marduk (556 BCE, Josephus Against Apion I.20)
nodes.role: Youthful Son of Neriglissar Deposed After Nine Months
nodes.notes: Son of Neriglissar and grandson of Nebuchadnezzar II; ruled nine months before conspirators raised Nabonidus to the throne.

nodes.name: King Nabonidus (Nabu-na'id, 556–539 BCE, Josephus Against Apion I.20)
nodes.era: 556–539 BCE (Josephus Against Apion I.20; Cyrus Cylinder)
nodes.role: Final Sovereign of Neo-Babylon
nodes.notes: Last Babylonian king (defeated by Cyrus the Great in 539 BCE); stationed in Tema while his eldest son Belshazzar governed Babylon.

nodes.name: Co-Regent Belshazzar (Son of Nabonidus, Dan 5)
nodes.role: Royal Co-Regent at the Fall of Babylon (539 BCE)
nodes.notes: Eldest son of Nabonidus and acting co-regent in Babylon on the night Cyrus's forces entered the city.

nodes.name: Esau / Edom = Rome & Byzantium Cross-Tradition Bridge (Josephus, Talmud, Jasher 60–61 Zepho/Janus & Al-Tabari Banu al-Asfar)
nodes.role: Classical Jewish & Islamic Identification of Rome/Byzantium With Esau (Edom)
nodes.notes: Explains why Jewish, Sefer ha-Yashar (Zepho/Janus king of Kittim/Rome), and early Islamic (Banu al-Asfar / al-Rum descended from Esau) traditions link Rome and Byzantium spiritually and genealogically to Esau.

nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.name: Adalia (Son 5 of Haman & Zeresh, Esth 9:9)
nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.role: Son of Haman the Agagite
nodes.notes: One of the ten named Amalekite sons of Haman ben Hammedatha and Zeresh slain at Susa.

nodes.name: King Areus I of Sparta (309–265 BCE; 1 Macc 12:21 & Josephus Ant. XII.4.10)
nodes.role: Spartan King Who Declared Spartans & Jews Brethren From Abraham
nodes.notes: Agiad King of Sparta whose sealed letter to High Priest Onias declared: 'It has been found in writing that the Spartans and the Jews are brethren, and that they are of the stock of Abraham!' Graduates classical Sparta into Biblically Connected!

nodes.name: Lawgiver Lycurgus of Sparta (Founder of Spartan Constitution)
nodes.era: c. 8th c. BCE (Herodotus; Plutarch Life of Lycurgus)
nodes.role: Traditional Lawgiver of Lacedaemon
nodes.notes: Established Sparta's dual kingship, Gerousia, and constitution praised by Josephus.

nodes.name: King Leonidas I of Sparta (Hero of Thermopylae, 480 BCE)
nodes.era: d. 480 BCE (Herodotus VII; Josephus Ant. XII.4.10)
nodes.role: Agiad King of Sparta (Graduated via Abraham–Sparta Charter)
nodes.notes: Agiad King of Sparta who fell defending Thermopylae with 300 Spartans; ancestor of King Areus I.

nodes.name: Queen Gorgo of Sparta (Daughter of Cleomenes I; Wife of Leonidas I)
nodes.role: Agiad Princess & Queen of Sparta
nodes.notes: Daughter of Agiad King Cleomenes I and wife of half-uncle King Leonidas I; mother of King Pleistarchus.

nodes.name: King Agesilaus II of Sparta (Eurypontid King, 400–360 BCE)
nodes.role: Eurypontid Spartan King & Commander in Asia Minor/Egypt
nodes.notes: Eurypontid King of Sparta who campaigned in Anatolia and Egypt.

nodes.name: King Cleomenes III of Sparta (Reformer Agiad King, 235–222 BCE)
nodes.role: Last Reformist Agiad King of Classical Sparta
nodes.notes: Son of Leonidas II (from Areus I's Agiad house) who revived Lycurgan reforms.

nodes.name: Daughter of Epher / Apher (Granddaughter of Abraham; Wife of Heracles, Cleodemus Malchus)
nodes.role: Midianite Granddaughter of Abraham Who Gave Africa Her Name & Wed Heracles
sources: Flavius Josephus Antiquities I.15 (quoting Alexander Polyhistor / Cleodemus Malchus)
nodes.notes: Josephus Ant. I.15 preserves Cleodemus Malchus: Abraham's grandson Epher/Apher conquered Libya (giving Africa its name) and gave his daughter in marriage to Heracles!

nodes.name: Diodorus (Son of Heracles & Apher's Daughter, Josephus Ant. I.15)
nodes.role: Son of Heracles & Abraham's Granddaughter
nodes.notes: Born to Heracles and Abraham's granddaughter (Apher's daughter); father of Sophax.

nodes.name: Sophax (Son of Diodorus; Founder of Tingis & Progenitor of Mauretanian Kings)
nodes.era: North African Horizon (Josephus Ant. I.15; Plutarch Sertorius 9)
nodes.role: Son of Diodorus & Ancestor of King Juba II
nodes.notes: Eponymous sovereign of Libya/Mauretania descended from Abraham via Keturah/Epher & Heracles; ancestor claimed by King Juba II.

nodes.name: King Juba II of Mauretania (+ Queen Cleopatra Selene II, d. 23 CE)
nodes.role: Scholar-King of Mauretania Claiming Descent From Heracles/Sophax
nodes.notes: Scholar-king of Mauretania (+ Cleopatra Selene, daughter of Cleopatra VII; later husband of Herodian widow Glaphyra!) claiming ancestry from Sophax -> Diodorus -> Heracles.

nodes.name: Princess Tharbis of Ethiopia (Meroe/Saba) — Wife of General Moses (Josephus Ant. II.10 pp.152–154)
nodes.role: Ethiopian Royal Daughter Married to Moses During Nile Campaign
nodes.notes: Josephus recounts how Moses commanded Egypt's army against Ethiopia using stork/ibis baskets against serpents, besieged Saba (Meroe), and wed Ethiopian royal princess Tharbis (matching the 'Cushite woman' of Numbers 12:1).

nodes.name: King Monobazus I (Bazeus) of Adiabene (Josephus Ant. XX.2.1)
nodes.era: c. 1–30 CE (Erbil / Adiabene — Josephus Ant. XX.2.1)
nodes.role: King of Adiabene & Husband of Sister-Queen Helena
nodes.notes: King of Adiabene (ancient Assyria/Erbil) and father of Kings Izates II and Monobazus II.

nodes.name: Queen Helena of Adiabene (Royal Convert Buried in Jerusalem, Josephus Ant. XX.2–4)
nodes.role: Queen Mother of Adiabene & Famine Benefactor of Jerusalem
nodes.notes: Converted to Judaism with her son King Izates II, fed Jerusalem during the famine of Acts 11:28, and built the monumental Tomb of the Kings in Jerusalem.

nodes.name: King Izates II of Adiabene (c. 36–60 CE, Josephus Ant. XX.2–4)
nodes.role: Convert King of Adiabene Circumcised & Allied With Parthia
nodes.notes: Son of Monobazus I & Queen Helena; married Symacho (daughter of King Abennerig of Charax Spasini) and fathered five sons educated in Jerusalem.

nodes.name: King Monobazus II of Adiabene (fl. 55–70 CE, Josephus Ant. XX.4.3)
nodes.era: fl. 55–70 CE (Adiabene — Josephus Ant. XX.4.3; Wars II.19.2)
nodes.role: Elder Brother & Successor of Izates II
nodes.notes: Elder brother of Izates II who also converted to Judaism and sent kinsmen Monobazus and Kenedeus to aid Jerusalem.

nodes.name: Intercultural Aliases of Abraham: Abram / Ibrahim (Arabic) / Berossus's 10th Chaldean / Cleodemus's Africa-Heracles / Spartan Kinsman / Brahma-Syncretic

I.7.2); Cleodemus's grandfather-in-law of Heracles & ancestor of Africa (Ant. I.15); Spartan kindred charter (1 Macc 12:21); and 17th-c. folkloric comparison of Abraham/Sarah <-> Brahma/Saraswati.

nodes.name: Intercultural Aliases of Moses: Moshe / Musa (Arabic) / Osarseph (Manetho) / Musaeus (Artapanus) / King of Cush (Jasher 73) / Husband of Tharbis (Josephus)
nodes.role: Unified Alias Index Across Bible, Egypt, Greece, Nubia & Arabia
sources: Josephus Ant. II.10 & Against Apion I.26
nodes.notes: Unites Moses's names across ancient accounts: Hebrew Moshe; Quranic Prophet Musa; Egyptian priest-chronicler Manetho's Osarseph; Greco-Jewish Artapanus's Musaeus (teacher of Orpheus & Hermes); Book of Jasher's 40-year King of Cush (+ Adoniah); and Josephus's victorious Egyptian general (+ Tharbis).

nodes.name: Intercultural Aliases of Noah: Noach / Nuh / Ziusudra (Sumer) / Utnapishtim (Atrahasis) / Xisuthros (Berossus) / Vaivasvata Manu (India) / Yima (Iran) / Deucalion (Greece) / Janus / Fuxi (Figurist)
nodes.role: Global Cognate & Parallel Hub Linking Humanity After the Deluge
nodes.notes: Side-by-side comparison showing Noah's exact equivalents/parallels: Sumerian Ziusudra, Akkadian Atrahasis/Utnapishtim, Berossus's Xisuthros, Indian Vaivasvata Manu, Avestan Yima, Greek Deucalion & Ogyges, 18th-c. Janus/Oenotrus (Betham/Anderson), and Jesuit Figurist Fuxi.

nodes.name: Intercultural Aliases of Enoch: Khanokh / Idris (Arabic) / Hermes Trismegistus / Thoth (Egypt) / King Saurid (Pyramid Builder) / Enmeduranki (7th Sage)
nodes.role: Greco-Egyptian, Coptic-Arabic & Mesopotamian 7th-Sage Matrix
nodes.notes: Tracks how the 7th Patriarch Enoch (inventor of writing & calendar in Jubilees 4:17) is identified in Coptic-Arabic chronicles with King Saurid (builder of Great Pyramids), in Hermeticism with Thoth/Hermes Trismegistus, in Islam with Prophet Idris, and compared structurally with Enmeduranki of Sippar.

nodes.name: Intercultural Aliases of Nimrod: Nebrod / Belus (Babylon) / Ninus (Assyria) / Al-Dahhak (Shahnameh) / Lamurudu (Yoruba Oduduwa Chronicle) / Orion
nodes.role: Near Eastern, Persian & West African Royal Syncretisms
sources: Samuel Johnson History of the Yorubas
nodes.notes: Maps Nimrod son of Cush across chronicles: Latin Vulgate/Dutripon Belus; classical Ninus of Nineveh; Persian/Arabic tyrants Zuhhak/Al-Dahhak (Tabari); and West African Yoruba chronicle ancestor Lamurudu -> Oduduwa.

nodes.name: Intercultural Aliases of Joseph & Solomon: Zaphenath-Paneah / Yusuf / Imhotep Parallel; Sulayman / King of Tadmor-Palmyra / Father of Menelik I (Ethiopia)
nodes.era: Egyptian Vizier & Near Eastern Sovereign Matrix
nodes.role: Biblical-Egyptian-Ethiopic-Palmyrene Royal Resonances
nodes.notes: Collects Joseph's Egyptian court title Zaphenath-Paneah (Arabic Yusuf, and 7-year-famine vizier parallel to Djoser's Imhotep) alongside Solomon (Sulayman), revered across Jerusalem, Aksumite Ethiopia (Menelik I), Yemen (Sheba/Bilqis), and Tadmor/Palmyra.
